title: Authentication contract
description: Language-neutral authentication entities shared by iOS, Android, backend, and admin. Native apps authenticate with the Firebase Authentication SDK directly; these definitions describe the canonical authenticated-user data the backend exposes (today via the frozen legacy /v1 REST API, in the target model via callable Cloud Functions such as auth.completeOnboarding). Backend is the source of truth for all auth and access decisions.

authIdentity.description: A linked sign-in identity. Provider subject is the stable identifier — email is intentionally absent.

providerSubject.description: Stable subject identifier issued by the provider.

onboardingStatus.description: Onboarding completion state. All timestamps are backend-written; null means the step has not been completed.

licenceConfirmedAt.description: When the member confirmed they hold a valid driving licence for the vehicle they drive.

ageConfirmedAt.description: LEGACY, read-only: when the member confirmed the earlier 18+ age wording. Superseded by licenceConfirmedAt — a different statement, so it is never migrated or rewritten. Non-null ONLY for a pre-change member who actually gave that confirmation; null for every member onboarded after the change AND for pre-change accounts that never completed the old onboarding (the stored field was seeded as null, and an absent field is also reported as null).

authenticatedUserSummary.description: Summary of the authenticated user returned by the backend. Backend is the source of truth — suspended/deleted users must not access protected features regardless of other fields.
